Josh Norris has five goals in 25 games for Buffalo, almost exactly what his chances say (4.62 expected goals, our measure of chance quality). His most recent came Wednesday, finishing a two-on-one from Josh Doan for what The Athletic's Matthew Fairburn called a "much-needed goal" from the third line. Between that and a two-goal night against Columbus on November 6, he went eight games without one.

The real luck story is everyone else. The Sabres have scored 9.1 fewer goals than their chances deserve with Norris on the ice, and our numbers flag that as the kind of thing that swings back. At five on five Buffalo has had an even 50% of the expected goals with him out there, so the process is sound. NHL EDGE has him among the league's fastest skaters, 94th percentile in top speed. He is playing just under 14 minutes a night, and Evolving-Hockey had him at 1.4 wins above replacement last season. Our numbers project 38 points, with room above that if his linemates' shooting comes back.
headline: Josh Norris, the Sabres' unlucky third-line center
